parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by specific latent heat.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A student determines the specific latent heat of vaporisation of a liquid using the apparatus illustrated in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:9702_w19_41_q03_figure_3_1}}

Fig. 3.1

The heater is switched on. When the liquid is boiling at a constant rate, the balance reading is noted at $2.0$ minute intervals.

After $10$ minutes, the current in the heater is reduced and the balance readings are taken for a further $12$ minutes.

The readings of the ammeter and of the voltmeter are given in Fig. 3.2.

{{figure:9702_w19_41_q03_figure_3_2}}

Fig. 3.2

The variation with time of the balance reading is shown in Fig. 3.3.

{{figure:9702_w19_41_q03_figure_3_3}}

Fig. 3.3

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
From time $0$ to time $10.0$ minutes, the mass of liquid evaporated is $56\text{ g}$.

Use Fig. 3.3 to determine the mass of liquid evaporated from time $12.0$ minutes to time $22.0$ minutes.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, although the power of the heater is changed, the rate of loss of thermal energy to the surroundings may be assumed to be constant.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine a value for the specific latent heat of vaporisation $L$ of the liquid.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Calculate the rate at which thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings.
